negative_findings.description: No civil-society or transparency-layer source was found that specifically tracks banking- or payments-sector procurement in North Macedonia. Targeted mk-language searching combining tender/contract terms with banking and IT/software terms ('истражувачко новинарство Македонија тендери банка договор', 'SCOOP Македонија Фокус Нова истражување тендер ИТ софтвер банка набавка') returned only generic ministry procurement pages, an investment story about a Bulgarian software firm, and unrelated media-funding polemics.
negative_findings.result_summary: The MK transparency/CSO layer is organised by institution and by corruption risk, not by economic sector. Banking and payments contracts must be extracted by filtering generic procurement datasets (CPV codes, buyer = NBRM and state-owned financial entities, supplier names), not by finding a sector-specific watchdog.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Sets expectations for the collection design: this cell yields horizontal datasets and analysis, and sector focus has to be imposed downstream by the collector, not sourced ready-made.

negative_findings.description: Broad mk-language queries using the natural local terms ('мониторинг на јавни набавки извештај НВО тендери Македонија', 'отворени податоци јавни набавки Македонија анализа договори') were dominated by ministry '/javni-nabavki' pages rather than by civil-society monitors. The CSO layer only surfaced once organisation names were used as query terms.
negative_findings.result_summary: Generic Macedonian procurement vocabulary is heavily polluted by the mandatory per-ministry procurement pages. Actor-name-anchored queries were required to reach the transparency layer.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Flags 'јавни набавки' as a noisy term for discovery and argues for an actor-first (name-anchored) discovery strategy in future MK passes for this cell.

negative_findings.description: IRL is described (in GIJN coverage and its own materials) as having built technical solutions for searching public databases more efficiently, but no publicly accessible procurement database or search tool operated by IRL was located in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: IRL's database tooling appears to be internal to the newsroom rather than a public asset; only its published stories were confirmed as accessible.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents over-crediting IRL as a data source. It should be tracked as a story/lead feed, and a direct approach would be needed to learn whether any tooling is shareable.

negative_findings.description: No established Macedonian-language equivalent of 'open contracting' / 'OCDS' was observed in any result. The mk-language framing is consistently 'јавните набавки како отворени податоци' (public procurement as open data), while OCDS/open-contracting terminology appears only in English-language sources (OCP registry, Opentender, OGP).
negative_findings.result_summary: Local-language discovery for the standards layer must use the descriptive Macedonian phrasing; the technical vocabulary is English-only in this jurisdiction.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A collector searching mk for 'отворено договарање' or transliterated OCDS terms will find nothing; the productive mk phrase is 'отворени податоци' + 'јавни набавки' / 'склучени договори'.

negative_findings.description: Several high-value URLs in this slice were obtained from link inventories or third-party coverage rather than from a successful direct fetch in this pass: javninabavki.opendata.mk, www.aktivnatransparentnost.mk, open.finance.gov.mk, transparentnost-mk.org.mk (http-only), and the e-nabavki.gov.mk InstitutionGridData.aspx endpoint.
negative_findings.result_summary: These are recorded as candidates with reduced confidence and access_status 'unverified'. No claim is made about their liveness.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The deterministic verification pass should prioritise these five; a 403 or timeout on any of them should be read as bot-defence, not death.

coverage_gaps.description: Albanian-language (sq) civil-society and media coverage of MK procurement was entirely out of scope for this run (languages were set to mk and en) and therefore uncovered. Albanian-language outlets and CSOs are a substantial part of the North Macedonian public sphere and monitor procurement in Albanian-majority municipalities.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add an sq-language pass using terms such as 'prokurimi publik', 'tenderë', 'kontrata publike', 'monitorimi i prokurimit publik' targeted at MK-based Albanian-language outlets and CSOs.

coverage_gaps.description: No commercial tender-aggregation or bid-alerting service for North Macedonia was properly assessed. One such vendor surfaced incidentally (selltostate.com listing an e-Nabavki agency feed) alongside generic 'Balkan tenders' listing sites, but their coverage, freshness and licensing were not evaluated.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated pass on commercial MK/Balkan tender-alert vendors; assess coverage depth, historical archive, export/API availability and terms of service before assuming they are usable.

coverage_gaps.description: Beyond CGK, the depth of the MK procurement-monitoring CSO field is unmapped. Umbrella and directory pointers were found (antikorupcija.mk members page, Civica Mobilitas grantee directory) but their member lists were not enumerated, so smaller and local watchdogs remain unknown.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Harvest the antikorupcija.mk members list and the Civica Mobilitas transparency/anti-corruption grantee listings, then run per-organisation checks for procurement outputs.

coverage_gaps.description: The actual coverage and freshness of the third-party structured datasets (Opentender MK, opendata.mk databases) relative to the official e-nabavki record was not measured. TED-derived data covers only above-threshold contracts, and MK is not an EU member, so the national-portal-derived share and its lag are decisive but unquantified.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Download the Opentender/OCP MK dataset and reconcile record counts and latest-award dates against a sample pulled from the official concluded-contracts export; document the lag and the value-threshold cut-off.

coverage_gaps.description: No archival/mirror strategy was identified for the CSO layer. NGO sites and donor-project sites (balkantenderwatch.eu in particular, a project site dating from 2012) are prone to link rot and hosting lapses once funding cycles end.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Mirror key CGK, Balkan Tender Watch and OSF policy PDFs at collection time and record Wayback Machine snapshots for each candidate URL in this slice.

brief: North Macedonia's procurement transparency layer has one clear centre of gravity: the Center for Civil Communications (ccc.org.mk), which is simultaneously the country's main monitoring NGO, the operator of the opendata.mk family of databases (Rationality Index, municipal procurement, million-euro and direct contracts), the national member of Balkan Tender Watch, and the publisher of the Active Transparency Index. Around it sit a machine-readable layer (Opentender MK via the Government Transparency Institute, registered in the OCP Data Registry; data.gov.mk; the Ministry of Finance's Otvoreni Finansii transaction portal), a policy layer that documents what data is promised and what is actually delivered (OGP commitments MK0073/MK0144/MK0146/MK0185, the national ovp.gov.mk portal, an OSF Western Balkans policy brief), and an investigative layer (IRL, Prizma/BIRN Macedonia) whose stories surface contract and ownership detail that notices never carry. The decisive limitation for this run's sector focus is that nothing in this layer is organised by industry: no banking- or payments-specific procurement monitor exists, so financial-sector contracts must be filtered out of horizontal datasets by buyer, CPV code and supplier name. Generic Macedonian procurement vocabulary is also noisy — searches for 'јавни набавки' are swamped by mandatory ministry pages — so discovery here works best anchored on actor names rather than topic terms.
